output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mainly an internal problem, not a Haverlow problem. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four on 27 July, night chilled pallets take about 3 h 50 min to reach the chambers, up from 44 min. Day receiving is unchanged. Staging lanes are unrefrigerated and sit at 15–17°C overnight. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, including Pellridge and own-label, while day rates stayed flat. Haverlow trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened. The 6.5–8°C receipt probe readings are keyed after the pallets have waited on the dock, so they don't show the temperature on arrival. Chambers held temperature. A chargeback and volume shift against Haverlow would punish the wrong party. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Next steps: restore night receiving to six, or otherwise cut dock-to-chamber time, and set a maximum time monitored weekly. Withdraw the chargeback notice. Separately, sample Corriebank's claims, because their self-certified credits rose after 3 August. Whether those claims are inflated is not established. Keep the night probe.
